001package org.clafer.ast;
002
003import java.util.ArrayDeque;
004import java.util.ArrayList;
005import java.util.Arrays;
006import java.util.Deque;
007import java.util.HashMap;
008import java.util.List;
009import java.util.Map;
010import java.util.stream.Collectors;
011import org.clafer.assertion.Assertion;
012import org.clafer.objective.Objective;
013
014/**
015 * Prints a model in a Clafer-like syntax with nothing left implicit: the
016 * clafers by their names (the compiler's UIDs), every card and group card,
017 * every {@code this}, {@code parent} and {@code dref}. The output is a Clafer
018 * model, which the Clafer compiler reads with {@code -f} (the names are already
019 * UIDs) and {@code -l} (no layout). Two models print the same when they have
020 * the same clafers, constraints, objectives and assertions, so the output can
021 * be compared, e.g., between two compilers of the same Clafer model. The
022 * scopes, all of them, go to the model's {@code .cfr-scope} file
023 * ({@link org.clafer.scope.ScopeFile}). The solver options (e.g., branching
024 * priorities) are not printed.
025 * <p>
026 * The clafers, their children and their constraints are printed in the order
027 * they were added, which is the order of the source and of the instances,
028 * abstract and concrete clafers interleaved (see {@link #sourceOrder}).
029 * Source spans are not printed.
030 * <p>
031 * Nesting is in braces, as in Clafer without layout: every clafer has its
032 * block, {@code {}} if it is empty. The indentation is only for reading;
033 * whitespace and line breaks carry no meaning.
034 * <p>
035 * Values are printed as they apply, declarations where they are declared. A
036 * group card and a multiplicity are values: a clafer without its own group
037 * card has its super clafer's, as chocosolver solves it, and {@code 0..*} if
038 * no super clafer has one; an abstract clafer's multiplicity is {@code 0..*}.
039 * Children, constraints and references are declarations: they stay under the
040 * clafer that declares them. A reference is printed only where it is declared
041 * or redefined, since in Clafer a reference written on a sub clafer redefines
042 * the inherited one, even with the same target.
043 * <p>
044 * Expressions are fully parenthesized, except for navigation ({@code .}),
045 * which binds tightest. {@code sum} and {@code product} take a set of clafers
046 * and add (multiply) the {@code dref} of each instance, so two instances with
047 * the same value count twice; this is printed as in Clafer, e.g.,
048 * {@code sum c0_Phone.c0_cost.dref}. An explicit dereference inside would
049 * print as {@code .dref.dref}.
050 */
051public class AstPrinter {
052
053    private static final String Indent = "  ";
054
055    private AstPrinter() {
056    }
057
058    /**
059     * The first line of an explicit model, which declares it to the Clafer
060     * compiler (its options -f -k -l --ss=none) and to chocosolver (read with
061     * {@link org.clafer.ast.ToAst}, not compiled by clafer).
062     */
063    public static final String ExplicitHeader = "//# OPTIONS --explicit";
064
065    /**
066     * Prints a model with its objectives and assertions, as an explicit model:
067     * {@link #ExplicitHeader}, then the model. Its scopes go to a separate
068     * file, see {@link org.clafer.scope.ScopeFile#print}.
069     *
070     * @param model the model
071     * @param objectives the objectives
072     * @param assertions the assertions
073     * @return the model as text, one line per clafer, constraint, objective
074     * and assertion
075     */
076    public static String print(AstModel model, Objective[] objectives, Assertion[] assertions) {
077        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
078        out.append(ExplicitHeader).append('\n');
079        out.append(print(model));
080        if (objectives.length > 0 || assertions.length > 0) {
081            out.append('\n');
082        }
083        for (Objective objective : objectives) {
084            out.append("<< ").append(objective.isMaximize() ? "max " : "min ")
085                    .append(print(objective.getExpr())).append(" >>\n");
086        }
087        for (Assertion assertion : assertions) {
088            out.append("assert [").append(print(assertion.getExpr())).append("]\n");
089        }
090        return out.toString();
091    }
092
093    /**
094     * Prints the clafers and constraints of a model.
095     *
096     * @param model the model
097     * @return the model as text
098     */
099    public static String print(AstModel model) {
100        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
101        AstAbstractClafer top = model.getAbstractRoot();
102        for (AstConstraint constraint : top.getConstraints()) {
103            printConstraint(constraint, "", out);
104        }
105        List<AstAbstractClafer> abstracts = top.getAbstractChildren().stream()
106                .filter(c -> c != model.getTypeRoot()).collect(Collectors.toList());
107        for (AstClafer clafer : sourceOrder(abstracts, top.getChildren())) {
108            printClafer(clafer, model, "", out);
109        }
110        // Constraints directly under root, as opposed to the top level, are
111        // possible in the Java API.
112        if (model.getRoot().hasConstraints()) {
113            out.append("root {\n");
114            for (AstConstraint constraint : model.getRoot().getConstraints()) {
115                printConstraint(constraint, Indent, out);
116            }
117            out.append("}\n");
118        }
119        return out.toString();
120    }
121
122    private static void printClafer(AstClafer clafer, AstModel model, String indent, StringBuilder out) {
123        out.append(indent);
124        if (clafer instanceof AstAbstractClafer) {
125            out.append("abstract ");
126        }
127        Card groupCard = AstUtil.getInheritedGroupCard(clafer);
128        out.append(groupCard == null ? "0..*" : card(groupCard)).append(' ');
129        out.append(clafer.getName());
130        if (clafer.hasSuperClafer() && clafer.getSuperClafer() != model.getTypeRoot()) {
131            out.append(" : ").append(clafer.getSuperClafer().getName());
132        }
133        // Only the clafer's own reference: an inherited one written here would redefine it.
134        AstRef ref = clafer.getRef();
135        if (ref != null) {
136            out.append(ref.isUnique() ? " -> " : " ->> ").append(ref.getTargetType().getName());
137        }
138        // An abstract clafer has no card of its own: its instances are those
139        // of the clafers that extend it.
140        out.append(' ').append(clafer instanceof AstConcreteClafer concrete ? card(concrete.getCard()) : "0..*");
141        if (!clafer.hasConstraints() && !clafer.hasAbstractChildren() && !clafer.hasChildren()) {
142            out.append(" {}\n");
143            return;
144        }
145        out.append(" {\n");
146        String inner = indent + Indent;
147        for (AstConstraint constraint : clafer.getConstraints()) {
148            printConstraint(constraint, inner, out);
149        }
150        for (AstClafer child : sourceOrder(clafer.getAbstractChildren(), clafer.getChildren())) {
151            printClafer(child, model, inner, out);
152        }
153        out.append(indent).append("}\n");
154    }
155
156    /**
157     * The abstract and concrete children of a clafer, which the model keeps
158     * apart, merged in the order of the source model. The order matters to
159     * the solver: a sub clafer's place among the subs of its super clafer
160     * numbers its instances. The model built from the source adds the subs in
161     * the order of the source, and a clafer without a super clafer stays among
162     * the subs of {@code #clafer#} in the order of creation; so a list of subs
163     * that holds clafers from the subtrees of two children tells which child
164     * came first. Without one, the order is not seen by the solver, and the
165     * abstract child comes first.
166     */
167    private static List<AstClafer> sourceOrder(List<AstAbstractClafer> abstracts, List<AstConcreteClafer> concretes) {
168        if (abstracts.isEmpty() || concretes.isEmpty()) {
169            List<AstClafer> one = new ArrayList<>(abstracts);
170            one.addAll(concretes);
171            return one;
172        }
173        // A topological sort of the siblings: each list keeps its order, and
174        // a list of subs orders an abstract and a concrete child. Without an
175        // order between two, the abstract child comes first.
176        List<AstClafer> siblings = new ArrayList<>(abstracts);
177        siblings.addAll(concretes);
178        int n = siblings.size();
179        List<List<Integer>> after = new ArrayList<>();
180        int[] before = new int[n];
181        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
182            after.add(new ArrayList<>());
183        }
184        int a = abstracts.size();
185        for (int k = 0; k + 1 < n; k++) {
186            if (k + 1 != a) {
187                after.get(k).add(k + 1);
188                before[k + 1]++;
189            }
190        }
191        for (int i = 0; i < a; i++) {
192            for (int j = a; j < n; j++) {
193                Boolean abstractFirst = before(siblings.get(i), siblings.get(j));
194                if (abstractFirst != null) {
195                    int from = abstractFirst ? i : j, to = abstractFirst ? j : i;
196                    after.get(from).add(to);
197                    before[to]++;
198                }
199            }
200        }
201        List<AstClafer> sorted = new ArrayList<>(n);
202        boolean[] placed = new boolean[n];
203        while (sorted.size() < n) {
204            // The first sibling, in the default order, that nothing must
205            // precede; if the orders contradict each other, the first left.
206            int next = -1;
207            for (int k = 0; k < n && next < 0; k++) {
208                if (!placed[k] && before[k] == 0) {
209                    next = k;
210                }
211            }
212            for (int k = 0; k < n && next < 0; k++) {
213                if (!placed[k]) {
214                    next = k;
215                }
216            }
217            placed[next] = true;
218            sorted.add(siblings.get(next));
219            for (int k : after.get(next)) {
220                before[k]--;
221            }
222        }
223        return sorted;
224    }
225
226    /**
227     * @return whether the subtree of a comes before the subtree of b in a list
228     * of subs that has clafers of both, or null if no list has
229     */
230    private static Boolean before(AstClafer a, AstClafer b) {
231        Map<AstClafer, Integer> firstOfB = new HashMap<>();
232        for (AstClafer y : subtree(b)) {
233            if (y.hasSuperClafer()) {
234                firstOfB.merge(y.getSuperClafer(), y.getSuperClafer().getSubs().indexOf(y), Math::min);
235            }
236        }
237        for (AstClafer x : subtree(a)) {
238            if (x.hasSuperClafer()) {
239                Integer other = firstOfB.get(x.getSuperClafer());
240                if (other != null) {
241                    return x.getSuperClafer().getSubs().indexOf(x) < other;
242                }
243            }
244        }
245        return null;
246    }
247
248    private static List<AstClafer> subtree(AstClafer clafer) {
249        List<AstClafer> subtree = new ArrayList<>();
250        Deque<AstClafer> todo = new ArrayDeque<>();
251        todo.push(clafer);
252        while (!todo.isEmpty()) {
253            AstClafer c = todo.pop();
254            subtree.add(c);
255            c.getAbstractChildren().forEach(todo::push);
256            c.getChildren().forEach(todo::push);
257        }
258        return subtree;
259    }
260
261    private static void printConstraint(AstConstraint constraint, String indent, StringBuilder out) {
262        String expr = print(constraint.getExpr());
263        out.append(indent).append(constraint.isHard() ? "[" + expr + "]" : "(" + expr + ")").append('\n');
264    }
265
266    private static String card(Card card) {
267        return card.getLow() + ".." + (card.hasHigh() ? Integer.toString(card.getHigh()) : "*");
268    }
269
270    /**
271     * Prints an expression.
272     *
273     * @param expr the expression
274     * @return the expression as text
275     */
276    public static String print(AstExpr expr) {
277        return switch (expr) {
278            case AstThis e -> "this";
279            case AstGlobal e -> e.type().getName();
280            case AstLocal e -> e.getName();
281            case AstChildRelation e -> e.childType().getName();
282            case AstParentRelation e -> "parent(" + e.parentRelation().getName() + ")";
283            case AstRefRelation e -> "dref(" + e.ref().getSourceType().getName() + ")";
284            case AstConstant e -> constant(e);
285            case AstDecimalConstant e -> e.value().toPlainString();
286            case AstStringConstant e -> string(e.value());
287            case AstJoin e -> operand(e.left()) + "." + step(e.right());
288            case AstJoinParent e -> operand(e.children()) + ".parent";
289            case AstJoinRef e -> operand(e.deref()) + ".dref";
290            case AstNot e -> "!" + operand(e.expr());
291            // -1 is a constant, so the negation of a number is -(1), and of
292            // -1 is -(-1) rather than --1, which reads as the difference --.
293            case AstMinus e -> "-" + (e.expr() instanceof AstConstant || e.expr() instanceof AstDecimalConstant
294                    ? "(" + print(e.expr()) + ")" : operand(e.expr()));
295            case AstCard e -> "#" + operand(e.set());
296            case AstSum e -> "sum " + operand(e.set()) + ".dref";
297            case AstProduct e -> "product " + operand(e.set()) + ".dref";
298            case AstMax e -> "max " + operand(e.set());
299            case AstMin e -> "min " + operand(e.set());
300            case AstLength e -> "length " + operand(e.string());
301            case AstInverse e -> "~" + operand(e.relation());
302            case AstTransitiveClosure e -> (e.reflexive() ? "*" : "^") + operand(e.relation());
303            case AstCompare e -> binary(e.left(), e.op().getSyntax(), e.right());
304            case AstSetTest e -> binary(e.left(), e.op().getSyntax(), e.right());
305            case AstMembership e -> binary(e.member(), e.op().getSyntax(), e.set());
306            case AstMod e -> binary(e.dividend(), "%", e.divisor());
307            case AstUnion e -> binary(e.left(), "++", e.right());
308            case AstDifference e -> binary(e.left(), "--", e.right());
309            case AstIntersection e -> binary(e.left(), "**", e.right());
310            case AstDomainRestriction e -> binary(e.domain(), "<:", e.relation());
311            case AstRangeRestriction e -> binary(e.relation(), ":>", e.range());
312            case AstArithm e -> nary(e.operands(), e.op() == AstArithm.Op.DecimalMul ? "*."
313                    : e.op() == AstArithm.Op.DecimalDiv ? "/." : e.op().getSyntax());
314            case AstBoolArithm e -> nary(e.operands(), e.op().getSyntax());
315            case AstConcat e -> "concat(" + print(e.left()) + ", " + print(e.right()) + ")";
316            case AstPrefix e -> "prefix(" + print(e.prefix()) + ", " + print(e.word()) + ")";
317            case AstSuffix e -> "suffix(" + print(e.suffix()) + ", " + print(e.word()) + ")";
318            case AstConnected e -> "connected(" + print(e.nodes()) + ", " + print(e.relation())
319                    + (e.directed() ? ", directed)" : ", undirected)");
320            case AstUpcast e -> "upcast(" + print(e.base()) + ", " + e.target() + ")";
321            case AstDowncast e -> "downcast(" + print(e.base()) + ", " + e.target() + ")";
322            case AstTernary e -> "if " + operand(e.antecedent()) + " then " + operand(e.consequent())
323                    + " else " + operand(e.alternative());
324            case AstIfThenElse e -> "if " + operand(e.antecedent()) + " then " + operand(e.consequent())
325                    + " else " + operand(e.alternative());
326            case AstQuantify e -> e.quantifier().getSyntax() + " "
327                    + Arrays.stream(e.decls()).map(AstPrinter::decl).collect(Collectors.joining(", "))
328                    + " | " + print(e.body());
329        };
330    }
331
332    private static String decl(AstDecl decl) {
333        return (decl.isDisjoint() ? "disj " : "")
334                + Arrays.stream(decl.getLocals()).map(AstLocal::getName).collect(Collectors.joining("; "))
335                + " : " + print(decl.getBody());
336    }
337
338    private static boolean isAtom(AstExpr expr) {
339        return switch (expr) {
340            case AstThis e -> true;
341            case AstGlobal e -> true;
342            case AstLocal e -> true;
343            case AstChildRelation e -> true;
344            case AstParentRelation e -> true;
345            case AstRefRelation e -> true;
346            case AstConstant e -> true;
347            case AstDecimalConstant e -> true;
348            case AstStringConstant e -> true;
349            case AstConcat e -> true;
350            case AstPrefix e -> true;
351            case AstSuffix e -> true;
352            case AstConnected e -> true;
353            case AstUpcast e -> true;
354            case AstDowncast e -> true;
355            default -> false;
356        };
357    }
358
359    private static boolean isNavigation(AstExpr expr) {
360        return expr instanceof AstJoin || expr instanceof AstJoinParent || expr instanceof AstJoinRef;
361    }
362
363    /**
364     * An operand of an operator: navigation binds tighter than any operator,
365     * so only the other compound expressions are parenthesized.
366     */
367    private static String operand(AstExpr expr) {
368        return isAtom(expr) || isNavigation(expr) ? print(expr) : "(" + print(expr) + ")";
369    }
370
371    /**
372     * The right of a navigation, parenthesized unless it is an atom.
373     */
374    private static String step(AstExpr expr) {
375        return isAtom(expr) ? print(expr) : "(" + print(expr) + ")";
376    }
377
378    private static String binary(AstExpr left, String op, AstExpr right) {
379        return operand(left) + " " + op + " " + operand(right);
380    }
381
382    private static String nary(AstExpr[] operands, String op) {
383        return Arrays.stream(operands).map(AstPrinter::operand).collect(Collectors.joining(" " + op + " "));
384    }
385
386    private static String constant(AstConstant constant) {
387        int[][] value = constant.value();
388        // The empty set, of any type, is Clafer's noclafer.
389        if (Arrays.stream(value).allMatch(column -> column.length == 0)) {
390            return "noclafer";
391        }
392        if (constant.type().isInt() && value.length == 1 && value[0].length == 1) {
393            return Integer.toString(value[0][0]);
394        }
395        String tuples = Arrays.stream(value).map(Arrays::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
396        return "{" + tuples + "} :: " + constant.type();
397    }
398
399    /**
400     * A string from Clafer is its literal, quotes and escapes included, e.g.,
401     * {@code "John"}, and chocosolver solves and prints it so; it is printed
402     * as it is. Other strings, from the Java API, are quoted and escaped.
403     */
404    private static String string(String value) {
405        if (value.length() >= 2 && value.startsWith("\"") && value.endsWith("\"")) {
406            return value;
407        }
408        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder("\"");
409        for (char c : value.toCharArray()) {
410            switch (c) {
411                case '"' -> out.append("\\\"");
412                case '\\' -> out.append("\\\\");
413                case '\n' -> out.append("\\n");
414                case '\t' -> out.append("\\t");
415                default -> {
416                    if (c < ' ' || c > '~') {
417                        out.append(String.format("\\u%04x", (int) c));
418                    } else {
419                        out.append(c);
420                    }
421                }
422            }
423        }
424        return out.append('"').toString();
425    }
426}
